AggregationTermInRequest.description: An object representing an individual term to be aggregated, e.g. a term corresponding to `sexAtBirth` or `diagnosis`. The `id` property is required and identifies the term to be aggregated, while the `filters` and `splits` properties are optional modifiers of the aggregation term. Note: The request object does not specifiy the property or scope of the aggregation.

id.description: The `id` of the aggregation term as provided by the beacon. It is used to select the aggregation term, _i.e._ usually corresponding to a property in the data model.

selectors.description: List of selectors to select specific values of the given property for aggregation, as a modifier of the aggregation term. For example, for an aggregation term of `diagnosis` selectors could be used to specify a subset of diagnoses to be aggregated.

AggregationsInRequest.description: An aggregation request object representing a single aggregation to be performed by

aggregationTerms.description: An array of `AggregationTermInRequest` objects representing the terms to be aggregated for a single aggregation, e.g. terms corresponding to `sexAtBirth` and `diagnosis`.

requestId.description: An optional id for the aggregation request, which can be used for tracking and logging purposes. This is not used by the beacon for processing the request but can be included in the response metadata.

rangeBounds.description: The limits of the range, representing inclusive lower bounds to exclusive upper bounds. When only one value is given, it represents the lower bound and the upper bound is considered unbounded. The format of the values should be consistent with the type of the property being split, e.g. ISO8601 durations for time intervals or numeric values for continuous numeric variables.

sortOrder.description: Integer to specify the intended order of splits. This is required to ensure the correct order of bins in the results, or for the client to be able to reconstruct the expected order in case any of the intermediate steps reorders them.

SplitForAggregation.description: A split item for partitioning the values during aggregation.

label.description: A human readable label for the bin resulting from the split.

sortOrder.description: Integer to specify the intended order of splits. This is required to ensure the correct order of bins in the results, or for the client to be able to reconstruct the expected order in case any of the intermediate steps reorders them.

splitValue.description: A value at which the split should occur in the properties value space. The format of the value should be consistent with the type of the property being split, e.g. ISO8601 durations for time intervals or numeric values for continuous numeric variables. Split values are exclusive upper bounds for the resulting bins, meaning that values equal to the split value will be included in the next bin. Note: To cover the complete value space one might use a (last) split value that extends beyond the maximum value in the data, e.g. `P150Y` for age at diagnosis.

ValueForAggregation.description: An object representing a specific value of the property on which the aggregation is performed, used as a modifier of the aggregation term to select specific values for aggregation. For example, for an aggregation term of `diagnosis` this could be used to specify a specific diagnosis to be aggregated.

label.description: An optional label for the value, e.g. to allow the service to return in an informative response.

value.description: The specific value of the category or value to be aggregated, e.g. an ontology term CURIE an alphanumeric value.

description:
Terms used to specify items to return in an aggregation data response. Terms
are provided through the beacon's `/aggregation_terms` endpoint and the `id`
values of those terms constitute the possible `id` values here. See also the
documentation for `AggregationTermInResponse.id` in `beaconAggregationTermsResults`.

* The `AggregationsInRequest` list is the list of all aggregations resulting
  in a distribution of one or more dimensional aggregation results.
* The individual aggregations have lists of 1 or more (but mostly 1 or 2)
  **aggregation terms**, usually corresponding to individual properties.
* If more than 1 aggregation term is provided it means that the corresponding
  properties should be evaluated together, e.g. all combinations of 
  "diagnoses (1) for sex at birth (2)".
* The individual aggregation terms can have modifiers to specify individual
  values or value ranges to be aggregated, e.g. selected diagnoses or age
  groups.
